exposure: Maternal age (15 and less, 16-19, and 20-34 years)
cohort: 1374 teenage pregnancies and 1294 adult pregnancies between January 2008 and December 2012, restricted to 1282 teenage pregnancies and 735 adult pregnancies after limiting analyses to singleton primiparous women
finding: Younger maternal age was correlated with increased risks of preterm delivery, fetal and neonatal death and anemia, while older maternal age was associated with higher rates of preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, chronic diseases, and IUGR.
mod_finding: Adolescents had a lower risk of cesarean delivery compared to older mothers.
